hero.name: Anmol Prabhakar
hero.focus: Focus: Electromechanical Integration, Mechanism Kinematics, and Wearable Biosensors

paragraphs: I build mechanical systems at the boundary where hardware interacts directly with the physical world and the human body. As a Bioengineering student with an Electrical Engineering minor, my focus is bridging mechanical kinematics with embedded control—from routing tendon channels and designing snap-fit linkages to reverse-engineering RF circuits and packaging wearable biosensors. I prioritize functional engineering: validating tight clearances in CAD, eliminating mechanism binding, and iterating prototypes to build responsive, reliable hardware.

bullets: Engineered modular EEG headset housings in Onshape using ISO shaft-basis interference fits (sub-0.03 mm clearances) and integrated friction detents with 0.4 mm engagement ribs, securing modular electrode cartridges against 3.5 N extraction loads without mechanical fasteners.
Routed internal 1.8 mm conduit pathways across 7 FDM iterations to prevent wire fatigue failure and reduced overall enclosure packaging volume by 25%.
Designed an adjustable compliant headband strap mechanism with 60 mm of travel, sustaining 1.5–2.0 N normal scalp contact pressure across head circumferences from 52 cm to 62 cm.

Evaluated analog front-end schematics and multi-pin cartridge interconnects to minimize contact impedance (<50 mΩ) and isolate microvolt biosignals (0.5–100 µV) from external electromagnetic interference (EMI).
Fabricated 13 custom-molded carbon fiber and polycarbonate orthotic inserts utilizing 25 in-Hg vacuum bagging and heated press lamination cycles (160°C–180°C).
Post-processed composite and thermoplastic blanks on a high-speed rotary grinder at 3,400 RPM, blending edge radii to sub-millimeter profiles to match strict internal shoe welt boundaries.

Digitized patient foot morphology with millimeter-level arch accuracy using flatbed optical surface scanners, and facilitated clinical delivery consultations via real-time Spanish translation for 20+ patients.
Assembled 8 adult and pediatric Knee-Ankle-Foot Orthoses (KAFOs) and cerebral palsy braces, mechanically aligning bilateral aluminum side-rails within 1° of the anatomical sagittal knee axis.
Calibrated drop-lock knee hinges to lock at 0° full extension, ensuring structural joint stability under 500+ N cyclic stance loads without binding.

Formed positive plaster limb casts to mold 3–4 mm rigid polycarbonate shells, and adjusted coronal and sagittal alignment angles across 10-meter patient walk tests to eliminate hyperextension hot spots.
